facts.statement: The animal is classified under the genus Deinonychus.
facts.quote: taxon: Deinonychus

facts.statement: The genus Deinonychus was described by John Ostrom in 1969.
facts.quote: authority: Ostrom, 1969

facts.statement: Deinonychus fossils date from the Early Cretaceous to the Late Cretaceous, specifically from the Aptian to Cenomanian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous-Late Cretaceous (Aptian to Cenomanian)

facts.statement: Deinonychus antirrhopus could grow up to 3.4 meters in length.
facts.quote: This species, which could grow up to 3.4 m long

facts.statement: The species lived approximately 115 to 98 million years ago during the Early and Late Cretaceous periods.
facts.quote: lived during the Early and Late Cretaceous Period, about 115–98 million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Deinonychus have been found in the U.S. states of Montana, Utah, Wyoming, and Oklahoma.
facts.quote: Fossils have been recovered from the U.S. states of Montana, Utah, Wyoming, and Oklahoma

facts.statement: John Ostrom described Deinonychus as having a small body, a sleek horizontal posture, a ratite-like spine, and enlarged raptorial claws on its feet.
facts.quote: Ostrom noted the small body, sleek, horizontal posture, ratite-like spine, and especially the enlarged raptorial claws on the feet

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with crocodile and bird claws, Ostrom reconstructed the claw of specimen YPM 5205 as being over 120 mm long.
facts.quote: Ostrom looked at crocodile and bird claws and reconstructed the claw for YPM 5205 as over 120 mm long

facts.statement: The species name antirrhopus means "counter balance" and refers to the proposed function of the tail.
facts.quote: The species name antirrhopus means "counter balance", which refers to Ostrom's idea about the function of the tail

facts.statement: Deinonychus remains found in the Cloverly and Antlers formations are closely associated with those of the ornithopod dinosaur Tenontosaurus.
facts.quote: In both the Cloverly and Antlers formations, Deinonychus remains have been found closely associated with those of the ornithopod Tenontosaurus

facts.statement: Teeth found associated with Tenontosaurus specimens suggest that Deinonychus hunted or scavenged from them.
facts.quote: Teeth discovered associated with Tenontosaurus specimens imply they were hunted, or at least scavenged upon, by Deinonychus

facts.statement: The first remains of Deinonychus were uncovered in 1931 in southern Montana near the town of Billings.
facts.quote: The first remains were uncovered in 1931 in southern Montana near the town of Billings

facts.statement: In August 1964, John Ostrom led an expedition from Yale's Peabody Museum of Natural History that discovered more skeletal material near Bridger.
facts.quote: A little more than thirty years later, in August 1964, paleontologist John Ostrom led an expedition from Yale's Peabody Museum of Natural History which discovered more skeletal material near Bridger

facts.statement: John Ostrom officially published his findings on Deinonychus in February 1969, having written the manuscript by December 1968.
facts.quote: Ostrom first wrote the manuscript by December 1968 and officially published his findings in February 1969

facts.statement: Ostrom's initial skeletal reconstruction included a very unusual pubis that was trapezoidal and flat.
facts.quote: Ostrom's skeletal reconstruction of Deinonychus included a very unusual pelvic bone—a pubis that was trapezoidal and flat

facts.statement: In 1974, Ostrom realized that the bone he had previously identified as a pubis was actually a coracoid, a shoulder element.
facts.quote: In 1974, Ostrom published another monograph on the shoulder of Deinonychus in which he realized that the pubis that he had described was actually a coracoid—a shoulder element

facts.statement: The discovery implies that Deinonychus used body heat transfer for egg incubation, indicating an endothermy similar to modern birds.
facts.quote: This implies that Deinonychus used body heat transfer as a mechanism for egg incubation, and indicates an endothermy similar to modern birds

facts.statement: Further study indicates that the individual specimen was 13 or 14 years old at death and had reached full growth.
facts.quote: Further study by Gregory Erickson and colleagues finds that this individual was 13 or 14 years old at death and its growth had plateaued

facts.statement: John Ostrom's 1969 description of Deinonychus is considered the most important single discovery in mid-20th-century dinosaur paleontology.
facts.quote: Ostrom's description of Deinonychus in 1969 has been described as the most important single discovery of dinosaur paleontology in the mid-20th century.

facts.statement: The discovery of Deinonychus as an active, agile predator helped shift scientific views on dinosaurs and sparked speculation that some were warm-blooded.
facts.quote: The discovery of this clearly active, agile predator did much to change the scientific (and popular) conception of dinosaurs and opened the door to speculation that some dinosaurs may have been warm-blooded.

facts.statement: John Ostrom revived the hypothesis that birds descended from dinosaurs after noting similarities between Deinonychus forefeet and bird feet.
facts.quote: Ostrom noted similarities between the forefeet of Deinonychus and that of birds, an observation which led him to revive the hypothesis that birds are descended from dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Based on mature specimens, Paul estimated Deinonychus reached 3.3 to 3.4 meters in length, had a 410 mm skull, 0.87 m hip height, and a mass of 60 to 73 kg.
facts.quote: Based on the few fully mature specimens, Paul estimated that Deinonychus could reach 3.3 - 3.4 m in length, with a skull length of 410 mm, a hip height of 0.87 m and a body mass of 60 - 73 kg.

facts.statement: Deinonychus had powerful jaws lined with approximately seventy curved, blade-like teeth.
facts.quote: The skull was equipped with powerful jaws lined with around seventy curved, blade-like teeth.

facts.statement: Deinonychus had a more robust skull roof similar to Dromaeosaurus and lacked the depressed nasals found in Velociraptor.
facts.quote: The skull of Deinonychus was different from that of Velociraptor, however, in that it had a more robust skull roof, like that of Dromaeosaurus, and did not have the depressed nasals of Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Deinonychus had a sickle-shaped claw on the second digit of each hind foot, likely used during predation.
facts.quote: Each hind foot bore a sickle-shaped claw on the second digit, which was probably used during predation.

facts.statement: No skin impressions have ever been found associated with Deinonychus fossils.
facts.quote: No skin impressions have ever been found in association with fossils of Deinonychus.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that Deinonychus and other dromaeosaurids were covered in feathers.
facts.quote: Nonetheless, the evidence suggests that the Dromaeosauridae, including Deinonychus, had feathers.

facts.statement: Deinonychus antirrhopus is a well-known dromaeosaurid species and a close relative of the smaller Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Deinonychus antirrhopus is one of the best known dromaeosaurid species, and also a close relative of the smaller Velociraptor, which is found in younger, Late Cretaceous-age rock formations in Central Asia.

facts.statement: Deinonychus and Velociraptor form a clade called Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: The clade they form is called Velociraptorinae.

facts.statement: A 2022 study reclassified Deinonychus as a basal member of Dromaeosaurinae.
facts.quote: A study in 2022, however, reclassified Deinonychus as a basal member of Dromaeosaurinae again.

facts.statement: In 2011, Denver Fowler proposed the 'raptor prey restraint' model, suggesting Deinonychus killed prey by leaping on it, pinning it with body weight, and gripping it with large sickle claws like eagles.
facts.quote: In 2011, Denver Fowler and colleagues suggested a new method by which Deinonychus and other dromaeosaurs may have captured and restrained prey. This model, known as the "raptor prey restraint" (RPR) model of predation, proposes that Deinonychus killed its prey in a manner very similar to extant accipitrid birds of prey: by leaping onto its quarry, pinning it under its body weight, and gripping it tightly with the large, sickle-shaped claws.

facts.statement: Deinonychus likely had a weak bite force and may have used sawing motions to finish off prey if its kicks were insufficient.
facts.quote: Its jaws, thought to have had a comparatively weak bite force, might be used for saw motion bites, like the modern Komodo dragon which also has a weak bite force, to finish off its prey if its kicks were not powerful enough.

facts.statement: Isotopic analysis suggests adult Deinonychus likely fed on Tenontosaurus to some degree.
facts.quote: Within the same year, isotopic analysis done by Frederickson and colleagues, found that adult Deinonychus were likely feeding on Tenontosaurus to some degree.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Deinonychus specialized on larger prey, as 2020 analysis of snout morphology suggests a short, deep maxilla resembling short-snouted canids.
facts.quote: In 2020, Powers and colleagues analyzed the snout morphology of dromaeosaurids from North America and Asia, their findings suggest that the maxilla of Deinonychus was short and deep, resembling that of short-snouted canids, suggesting that Deinonychus specialized on larger prey.

facts.statement: Studies based on tooth puncture marks estimated Deinonychus bite force between 4,100 and 8,200 newtons, exceeding that of hyenas and matching similarly sized alligators.
facts.quote: They found the bite force of Deinonychus to be between 4,100 and 8,200 newtons, greater than living carnivorous mammals including the hyena, and equivalent to a similarly-sized alligator.

facts.statement: A 2022 study using a skull estimated Deinonychus bite force at 706 N, contradicting earlier higher estimates based on bite marks.
facts.quote: However, this estimate has come into question, as it was based on bite marks rather than a Deinonychus skull. A recent 2022 study used a Deinonychus skull for their estimate and calculated 706 N.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Deinonychus likely used its strong bite for defense or capturing prey rather than for feeding on bone.
facts.quote: Instead, they probably used their strong bite force for defense or to capture prey, rather than for feeding.

facts.statement: It is suggested that Deinonychus may have used neck-driven pullback movements to dismember carcasses, similar to modern varanid lizards.
facts.quote: It is also suggested in these findings that Deinonychus may have fed by using neck-driven pullback movements to dismember carcasses when feeding, akin to modern varanid lizards.

facts.statement: Some studies suggest Deinonychus sickle claws were used to deliver small stabs rather than to slash prey.
facts.quote: Other studies have suggested that the sickle claws were not used to slash but rather to deliver small stabs to the victim.

facts.statement: A 2011 study suggested Deinonychus used its sickle claw to pin down prey while biting, rather than as a slashing weapon.
facts.quote: In 2011, a study suggested that the sickle claw would likely have been used to pin down prey while biting it, rather than as a slashing weapon.

facts.statement: Biomechanical studies confirmed Deinonychus forelimbs were likely used for grasping prey due to their length allowing greater reach than most other theropods.
facts.quote: Biomechanical studies by Ken Carpenter in 2002 confirmed that the most likely function of the forelimbs in predation was grasping, as their great lengths would have permitted longer reach than for most other theropods.

facts.statement: Research from 2006 suggests Deinonychus could use its forelimbs to clutch objects against its chest.
facts.quote: Studies by Phil Senter in 2006 indicated that Deinonychus forelimbs could be used not only for grasping, but also for clutching objects towards the chest.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Alan Gishlick found that Deinonychus could grasp objects effectively even if it had large wing feathers.
facts.quote: Alan Gishlick, in a 2001 study of Deinonychus forelimb mechanics, found that even if large wing feathers were present, the grasping ability of the hand would not have been significantly hindered

facts.statement: A 2001 examination of 43 hand bones and 52 foot bones found no signs of stress fractures in Deinonychus.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, 43 hand bones and 52 foot bones referred to Deinonychus were examined for signs of stress fracture; none were found.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from specimen YPM 5205 reveals a healed fracture on the second phalanx of the second toe.
facts.quote: The second phalanx of the second toe in the specimen YPM 5205 has a healed fracture.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest juvenile Deinonychus may have had more curved claws than adults to assist in climbing trees.
facts.quote: Parsons and Parsons have suggested that the claw curvature (which Ostrom [1976] had already shown was different between specimens) maybe was greater for juvenile Deinonychus, as this could help it climb in trees

facts.statement: A 2015 analysis of immature fossils suggests young Deinonychus might have been capable of some form of flight due to their mobile shoulder joints.
facts.quote: In a 2015 paper, it was reported after further analysis of immature fossils that the open and mobile nature of the shoulder joint might have meant that young Deinonychus were capable of some form of flight.

facts.statement: A 2016 study found Deinonychus scored -2.2 on cursoriality metrics, suggesting it could not maintain high speeds for extended periods.
facts.quote: In 2016, Scott Persons IV and Currie examined the limb proportion of numerous theropods and found Dromaeosaurids weren't cursorial animals due to their low CLP scores, with Deinonychus scoring -2.2

facts.statement: A probable Deinonychus egg was identified in 2000 and found associated with one of the original specimens of the animal.
facts.quote: The identification, in 2000, of a probable Deinonychus egg associated with one of the original specimens allowed comparison with other theropod dinosaurs in terms of egg structure, nesting, and reproduction.

facts.statement: Research suggests the egg was intact beneath the Deinonychus body when it was buried, indicating possible brooding or nesting behavior.
facts.quote: All the evidence, according to Grellet-Tinner and Makovicky, indicates that the egg was intact beneath the body of the Deinonychus when it was buried.

facts.statement: Based on the width of the pelvic canal, researchers estimated the diameter of the Deinonychus egg to be about 7 cm.
facts.quote: While the egg was too badly crushed to accurately determine its size, Grellet-Tinner and Makovicky estimated a diameter of about 7 cm based on the width of the pelvic canal through which the egg had to have passed.

facts.statement: A 2018 study indicates that Deinonychus laid blue eggs, likely for camouflage and open nesting.
facts.quote: A study published in November 2018 by Norell, Yang and Wiemann et al., indicates that Deinonychus laid blue eggs, likely to camouflage them as well as creating open nests.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Deinonychus was a gregarious animal.
facts.quote: Scientists have debated whether or not Deinonychus was gregarious.

facts.statement: The association of multiple Deinonychus skeletons with Tenontosaurus fossils suggests the predator may have hunted its prey.
facts.quote: The association of this number of Deinonychus skeletons in a single quarry suggests that Deinonychus may have fed on that animal, and perhaps hunted it.

facts.statement: A Tenontosaurus humerus fossil bears marks that might be tooth marks from Deinonychus.
facts.quote: One tenontosaur humerus even bears what might be Deinonychus tooth marks.

facts.statement: Brinkman et al. noted that adult Deinonychus weighed 70 to 100 kg, while adult Tenontosaurus weighed 1 to 4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Brinkman et al. (1998) point out that Deinonychus had an adult mass of 70 – 100 kg, whereas adult tenontosaurs were 1–4 metric tons.

facts.statement: A 2007 study by Roach and Brinkman questioned the cooperative pack hunting behavior of Deinonychus, suggesting a solitary feeding strategy similar to Komodo dragons.
facts.quote: A 2007 study by Roach and Brinkman has called into question the gregariousness and cooperative pack hunting behavior of Deinonychus, based on what the authors assumed about modern carnivore hunting and the taphonomy of tenontosaur sites.

facts.statement: Currie and Eberth criticized the 2007 study, arguing that gregarious carnivores can be intolerant of each other while still exhibiting complex social behavior.
facts.quote: Currie and Eberth criticized Roach and Brinkman (2007) in their 2010 paper, pointing out that many gregarious carnivores are very intolerant towards conspecifics yet still develop complex, social behavior.

facts.statement: Carbon isotope analysis of teeth suggests that Deinonychus hatchlings were precocial.
facts.quote: A carbon isotopic analysis on Deinonychus teeth suggests precociality in the genus.

facts.statement: Isotopic evidence indicates that adults and juveniles of Deinonychus had different diets.
facts.quote: The isotopes found for different aged specimens indicate that adults and juveniles had different diets across the various age groups

facts.statement: Examinations suggest that Deinonychus did not engage in mammal-like pack hunting.
facts.quote: The examinations also suggests a lack of mammal-like pack hunting in Deinonychus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Deinonychus was likely gregarious with social tolerance comparable to crocodilians.
facts.quote: Despite this, due to the lack of spatial separation of juvenile and adults, Deinonychus was likely gregarious, having social tolerance at least that of crocodilians

facts.statement: Researchers argue that Deinonychus was likely not monogamous and practiced ratite-like parental care.
facts.quote: They argued due to some adults having overlapping values with smaller individuals, Deinonychus probably was not monogamous and instead practiced ratite-like parental care.

facts.statement: Geological evidence suggests Deinonychus inhabited floodplain or swamplike habitats.
facts.quote: Paleoenvironment Geological evidence suggests that Deinonychus inhabited a floodplain or swamplike habitat.

facts.statement: The middle portion of the Cloverly Formation, where Deinonychus remains are found, ranges in age from 115 ± 10 Ma to 93 ± 8 Ma.
facts.quote: The middle portion of the Cloverly Formation ranges in age from 115 ± 10 Ma near the base to 93 ± 8 Ma near the top.

facts.statement: During the Albian, much of North America was blanketed by vast forests with diverse plant life.
facts.quote: During the Albian, much of North America was blanketed by vast forests composed of diverse plant life.

facts.statement: Deinonychus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Inferior

facts.statement: The genus Deinonychus was described by Ostrom in 1969.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Ostrom, 1969

facts.statement: The species D. antirrhopus was described by Ostrom in 1969.
facts.quote: species_authority: Ostrom, 1969

facts.statement: Deinonychus antirrhopus is the only species in the extinct genus Deinonychus, a coelurosaurian dromaeosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Deinonychus antirrhopus (gr. «Garra terrible con contrapeso») es la única especie del género extinto Deinonychus de dinosaurio celurosauriano dromeosáurido

facts.statement: Deinonychus lived approximately 115 to 108 million years ago between the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió hace unos 115 a 108 millones de años entre el Aptiano al Albiano a mediados del período Cretácico Inferior, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: This species could grow up to 3.4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Esta especie podría crecer hasta 3,4 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Fossils have been recovered from the US states of Montana, Utah, Wyoming, and Oklahoma.
facts.quote: Los fósiles se han recuperado de los estados de Estados Unidos de Montana, Utah, Wyoming y Oklahoma

facts.statement: Teeth that may belong to Deinonychus have also been found further east in Maryland.
facts.quote: aunque los dientes que pueden pertenecer a Deinonychus han sido encontrados mucho más al este, en Maryland.

facts.statement: John Ostrom's study of Deinonychus in the late 1960s revolutionized how scientists thought about dinosaurs.
facts.quote: El estudio del paleontólogo John Ostrom de Deinonychus realizado a finales de la década de 1960 revolucionó la manera como los científicos pensaban acerca de los dinosaurios

facts.statement: Ostrom observed Deinonychus as having a small, elegant body with a horizontal posture, a stiffened spine, and notably enlarged sickle-shaped claws on its feet.
facts.quote: Ostrom observó el cuerpo pequeño, elegante, de postura horizontal, columna vertebral estrucioniforme, y sobre todo las garras rapaces agrandadas en los pies

facts.statement: The genus name means 'terrible claw', referring to the unusually large, sickle-shaped claw on the second toe of each hind foot.
facts.quote: El significado del nombre del género, «Garra terrible», se refiere a la garra inusualmente grande, en forma de hoz en el segundo dedo de cada pata trasera.

facts.statement: Ostrom reconstructed the claw for specimen YPM 5205 to be over 120 millimeters long based on observations of crocodiles and bird claws.
facts.quote: Ostrom observó cocodrilos y garras de aves y reconstruyó la garra para YPM 5205 de más de 120 milímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The species name antirrhopus means 'counterbalance', referring to Ostrom's idea of the tail's function.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie antirrhopus significa "contrapeso", que se refiere a la idea de Ostrom sobre la función de la cola.

facts.statement: These features suggest that the tail was a rigid counterbalance.
facts.quote: Estas características hacen suponer que la cola sea un contrapeso rígido

facts.statement: Remains of Deinonychus have been found closely associated with those of the ornithopod Tenontosaurus in the Cloverly and Antlers formations.
facts.quote: Tanto en las formaciones de Cloverly como de Antlers, se han encontrado restos de Deinonychus estrechamente asociados con las del ornitópodo Tenontosaurus.

facts.statement: Teeth found associated with Tenontosaurus specimens imply that these animals were hunted, or at least formed part of Deinonychus's diet as carrion.
facts.quote: Los dientes descubiertos asociados a especímenes de Tenontosaurus implica que estos eran cazados, o al menos formaban parte declaraciones dieta en forma de carroña, de Deinonychus.

facts.statement: Based on few fully mature specimens, Deinonychus could reach 3.4 meters in length, with a skull around 410 millimeters, a hip height of 87 centimeters, and a weight of 73 kg.
facts.quote: Basado en los pocos ejemplares completamente maduros, Deinonychus podría alcanzar los 3,4 metros de largo, con un cráneo de alrededor de 410 milímetros, una altura de 87 centímetros a las caderas y un peso de 73 kg

facts.statement: However, there are higher estimates of weight up to 100 kg.
facts.quote: aunque hay estimaciones más altas de hasta 100 kg.

facts.statement: The skull was equipped with powerful jaws lined with around seventy blade-like curved teeth.
facts.quote: El cráneo estaba equipado con poderosas mandíbulas bordeadas de alrededor de setenta dientes como cuchillas curvas.

facts.statement: Ostrom reconstructed the skull from partial, imperfectly preserved specimens, describing them as triangular, broad, and quite similar to Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Ostrom lo reconstruyó a partir de ejemplares parciales, preservados imperfectamente, describiéndolos como triangulares, amplios, y bastante similares a los del Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Additional skull material and closely related genera found with good three-dimensional preservation show that the palate was more domed, making it narrower than Ostrom thought.
facts.quote: Material adicional del cráneo de Deinonychus y géneros estrechamente vinculados encontrados con una buena preservación tridimensional muestran que el paladar estaba más abovedado volviéndolo más estrecho que lo que pensó Ostrom

facts.statement: The Deinonychus skull differed in shape from Velociraptor, having a cranial vault like Dromaeosaurus and lacking the depressed nasals of Velociraptor.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Deinonychus era diferente en la forma al de Velociraptor, con una bóveda craneana como la de Dromaeosaurus, y no tenía los nasales deprimidos de Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Both the skull and lower jaw had fenestrae, skull openings, that reduced the weight of the skull.
facts.quote: Tanto el cráneo como la mandíbula inferior tenían fenestras, aberturas de cráneo, que reducían el peso del cráneo.

facts.statement: In Deinonychus, the anteorbital window, an opening in the skull between the eye and nostrils, was particularly large.
facts.quote: En Deinonychus la ventana anteorbital, una abertura del cráneo entre el ojo y las narinas, eran particularmente grandes.

facts.statement: Michael Crichton chose to use the name Velociraptor instead of Deinonychus for his novels after meeting with John Ostrom to discuss the dinosaur's behavior and appearance.
facts.quote: Crichton ultimately chose to use the name Velociraptor for these dinosaurs, rather than Deinonychus. Crichton had met with John Ostrom several times during the writing process to discuss details of the possible range of behaviors and life appearance of Deinonychus.

facts.statement: Jurassic Park filmmakers designed their models based almost entirely on Deinonychus rather than the actual Velociraptor.
facts.quote: The Jurassic Park filmmakers followed suit, designing the film's models based almost entirely on Deinonychus instead of the actual Velociraptor

facts.statement: It is debated whether Deinonychus had a complete agonistic relationship like Komodo dragons or was gregarious with social tolerance at least that of crocodilians.
facts.quote: Despite this, due to the lack of spatial separation of juvenile and adults, Deinonychus was likely gregarious, having social tolerance at least that of crocodilians, instead of a complete agonistic relationship as seen in Komodo dragons.

facts.statement: Deinonychus had large forelimbs with three claws on each hand.
facts.quote: Deinonychus poseía grandes "manos" con tres garras en cada extremidad delantera.

facts.statement: The first digit of the forelimb was shorter than the second digit.
facts.quote: El primer dígito era más corto y el segundo era más largo.

facts.statement: Each hind foot had a sickle-shaped claw on the second digit, likely used during predation.
facts.quote: Cada pata trasera llevaba una garra en forma de hoz en el segundo dígito, lo que probablemente fuese utilizada durante la depredación.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that Dromaeosaurids, including Deinonychus, had feathers.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la evidencia sugiere que los Dromaeosauridae, incluyendo Deinonychus, tenían plumas.

facts.statement: Multiple Microraptor fossils preserve pennaceous feathers with vanes like modern birds on arms, legs, and tail, along with covert and contour feathers.
facts.quote: Múltiples fósiles de Microraptor preservan plumas pennáceas, o sea, plumas con álabes como las de las aves modernas en los brazos, las piernas y la cola, junto con plumas encubiertas y de contorno.

facts.statement: A Velociraptor specimen was found with feather insertion bumps on the ulna.
facts.quote: Un espécimen de Velociraptor se ha encontrado con las perillas de inserción de plumas en el cúbito.

facts.statement: Deinonychus fossils have been recovered from the Cloverly Formation in Montana and Wyoming and the Antlers Formation in Oklahoma, North America.
facts.quote: Los restos fosilizados de Deinonychus han sido recuperados de la formación Cloverly de Montana y Wyoming y en la formación Antlers de Oklahoma, en América del Norte.

facts.statement: The Cloverly Formation is dated to the late Aptian to early Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, around 115 to 108 million years ago.
facts.quote: La formación Cloverly ha sido fechada a finales del Aptiano tomando como referencia las primeras etapas de Albiano del Cretácico temprano, alrededor de 115 a 108 Ma.

facts.statement: The first remains were found in 1931 in southeastern Montana near the town of Billings.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos en ser encontrados, se hallaron en 1931 en el sudeste de Montana cerca del pueblo de Billings.

facts.statement: Brown informally named the animal "Daptosaurus agilis", prepared it for display under catalog number AMNH 3015, but never finished the work.
facts.quote: Brown llamó informalmente al animal "Daptosaurus agilis" e hizo preparaciones para describirlo y lo colocó en la exhibición, bajo el número de catálogo AMNH 3015, pero nunca terminó este trabajo.

facts.statement: Later, B. Brown returned from the Cloverly Formation with a smaller theropod skeleton with large teeth, which he informally named "Megadontosaurus".
facts.quote: Posteriormente B. Brown volvió de la Formación Cloverly con el esqueleto de un terópodo más pequeño con aparentemente los dientes de gran tamaño, al que nombró informalmente como "Megadontosaurus".

facts.statement: John Ostrom reviewed the material decades later, identifying the teeth as belonging to a Deinonychus and the skeleton as a distinct animal he named Microvenator.
facts.quote: John Ostrom revisó el material varias décadas más tarde, identificando a los dientes como pertenecientes a un Deinonychus y el esqueleto proveniente de un animal totalmente distinto al que nombró Microvenator.

facts.statement: In August 1964, paleontologist John Ostrom led a Yale Peabody Museum expedition that discovered more skeletal material.
facts.quote: Un poco más de treinta años más tarde, en agosto de 1964, el paleontólogo John Ostrom llevó a una expedición del Museo Peabody de la Universidad de Yale que descubrió más material esquelético.

facts.statement: Expeditions over the following two summers unearthed over a thousand bones, including at least three individuals.
facts.quote: Las expediciones durante los dos veranos siguientes desenterraron más de mil huesos, entre los cuales estaban por lo menos tres individuos.

facts.statement: Because the association between recovered bones was weak, the type specimen YPM 5205 was restricted to a complete left foot and a partial right foot that definitely belonged to the same individual.
facts.quote: Puesto que la asociación entre los varios huesos recuperados era débil, fue imposible determinar cual era el número exacto de animales individuales, el espécimen tipo, YPM 5205, de Deinonychus fue restringido a un pie izquierdo completo y un pie derecho parcial que pertenecieron definitivamente al mismo individuo.

facts.statement: J. Ostrom published his discovery in 1969, assigning all referred remains the name Deinonychus antirrhopus.
facts.quote: J. Ostrom publicó su descubrimiento en 1969, dándole a todos los restos referido al nombre de Deinonychus antirrhopus.

facts.statement: The genus name means 'terrible claw' in Greek.
facts.quote: El nombre del género significa δεινός, 'terrible' y , con el genitivo 'garra'.

facts.statement: The specific name "antirrhopus" means "counterbalance" in Greek and refers to the probable effects of a rigid tail.
facts.quote: El nombre específico "antirrhopus", del griego ἀντίρροπος significa "contrapeso" y se refiere a los probables efectos probables de una cola rígida.

facts.statement: In July 1969, Ostrom published an extensive monograph on Deinonychus.
facts.quote: En julio de 1969, Ostrom publicó una extensa monografía sobre Deinonychus.

facts.statement: J. Ostrom's skeletal reconstruction of Deinonychus included an unusual pelvic bone, a trapezoidal and flat pubis, different from other theropods but of the same length as the ischium and located next to it.
facts.quote: La reconstrucción esquelética de J. Ostrom de Deinonychus incluyó un hueso pélvico muy inusual, un pubis trapezoidal y plano, diferente al de los otros terópodos, pero que era de la misma longitud que el isquion y que se encontraba junto a este.

facts.statement: In 1974, Ostrom published another monograph on the shoulder of Deinonychus, correcting that the pubis he described was actually a coracoid, a shoulder element.
facts.quote: En 1974 Ostrom publicó otra monografía sobre el hombro de Deinonychus, en la cual corrigió que el pubis que él había descrito era realmente un coracoides, un elemento del hombro.

facts.statement: That same year, another Deinonychus specimen was excavated in Montana by a Harvard University expedition led by Farish Jenkins.
facts.quote: En ese mismo año, otro espécimen de Deinonychus fue excavado en Montana por una expedición de la Universidad de Harvard dirigida por Farish Jenkins.

facts.statement: This discovery added several new elements such as well-preserved femurs, pubis, a sacrum, better ilia, as well as foot and metatarsal elements.
facts.quote: Este descubrimiento agregó varios nuevos elementos como fémures bien preservados, pubis, un sacro y mejores iliones, así como los elementos del pie y del metatarso.

facts.statement: Ostrom described this specimen and revised the skeletal restoration of Deinonychus. This time very long pubis were seen, and Ostrom began to suspect they might have been oriented slightly backward like in birds.
facts.quote: Ostrom describió este espécimen y revisó la restauración esquelética de Deinonychus. Esta vez se vieron pubis muy largos, y Ostrom comenzó a sospechar que pudieron incluso haber estado orientados hacia atrás un poco como en las aves.

facts.statement: An examination of unprepared blocks by Gerald Grellet-Tinner and Peter Makovicky in 2000 revealed an interesting, previously overlooked feature.
facts.quote: Un examen de estos bloques sin preparación de Gerald Grellet-Tinner y de Peter Makovicky en 2000 reveló una característica interesante, pasada por alto.

facts.statement: Several long, thin bones identified as ossified tendons that helped rigidify Deinonychus's tail were actually gastralia, abdominal ribs.
facts.quote: Varios huesos largos y finos identificados en los bloques como tendones osificados, estructuras que ayudaron a volver rígida la cola de Deinonychus resultaron ser realmente gastralias, costillas abdominales.

facts.statement: Most significantly, a large amount of previously unnoticed fossilized eggshells were discovered in the rock matrix surrounding the original Deinonychus specimen.
facts.quote: Pero lo más significativo , una gran cantidad de cáscaras de huevo fosilizadas previamente inadvertidas fueron descubiertas en la matriz de la roca que había rodeado el espécimen original de Deinonychus.

facts.statement: Grellet-Tinner and Makovicky concluded the eggs almost certainly belonged to Deinonychus, representing the first identified dromaeosaurid egg.
facts.quote: Grellet-Tinner y Makovicky concluyeron que los huevos pertenecieron casi ciertamente a Deinonychus, representando el primer huevo del dromeosáurido que se identificara.

facts.statement: The external surface of an eggshell was found in close contact with gastralia, suggesting this Deinonychus may have been incubating its eggs.
facts.quote: Por otra parte, la superficie externa de una cáscara de huevo fue encontrada en contacto cercano con las gastralias que sugeriría que este Deinonychus pudo haber estado incubando sus huevos.

facts.statement: This implies Deinonychus performed body heat transfer as a mechanism for egg incubation, indicating endothermy similar to modern birds.
facts.quote: Esto implica que Deinonychus realizaba un traspaso térmico del cuerpo como mecanismo para la incubación del huevo, e indica endotermia similar a las aves actuales.

facts.statement: Additional study by Gregory Erickson and colleagues found this individual was between 13 and 14 years old at death and its growth had stopped.
facts.quote: El estudio adicional de Gregory Erickson y colegas encuentra que este individuo tenía entre 13 o 14 años a la muerte y su crecimiento se había detenido.

facts.statement: Unlike other theropods, in specimens found associated with eggs or nests, growth had ceased at the time of death.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros terópodos, en su estudio de los especímenes encontrados asociado con los huevos o nidos, había acabado el crecimiento a la hora de su muerte.

facts.statement: Bones identified as ossified tendons that helped rigidify Deinonychus's tail were actually gastralia, abdominal ribs.
facts.quote: Varios huesos largos y finos identificados en los bloques como tendones osificados, estructuras que ayudaron a volver rígida la cola de Deinonychus resultaron ser realmente gastralias, costillas abdominales.

facts.statement: An eggshell surface was found in close contact with gastralia, suggesting this Deinonychus may have been incubating its eggs.
facts.quote: la superficie externa de una cáscara de huevo fue encontrada en contacto cercano con las gastralias que sugeriría que este Deinonychus pudo haber estado incubando sus huevos.

facts.statement: This implies Deinonychus performed body heat transfer for egg incubation, indicating endothermy similar to modern birds.
facts.quote: Esto implica que Deinonychus realizaba un traspaso térmico del cuerpo como mecanismo para la incubación del huevo, e indica endotermia similar a las aves actuales.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the identified eggs definitely belonged to Deinonychus, though researchers concluded they almost certainly did.
facts.quote: Grellet-Tinner y Makovicky concluyeron que los huevos pertenecieron casi ciertamente a Deinonychus, representando el primer huevo del dromeosáurido que se identificara.

facts.statement: Deinonychus is one of the best-known dromaeosaurids, closely related to the small Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Deinonychus es uno de los mejor conocidos entre los Dromaeosauridae, junto al más pequeño y relativamente cercano Velociraptor

facts.statement: Deinonychus and Velociraptor form a clade named Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: El clado que ellos forman se llama Velociraptorinae

facts.statement: The name Velociraptorinae was first coined by Rinchen Barsbold in 1983.
facts.quote: El nombre Velociraptorinae fue acuñado por primera vez por Rinchen Barsbold en 1983

facts.statement: Along with Troodontidae, dromaeosaurids of the clade Deinonychosauria are sister taxa to birds.
facts.quote: Junto con Troodontidae, los dromeosáuridos del clado Deinonychosauria son taxones hermanos de las aves

facts.statement: Phylogenetically, Deinonychosauria is the group of non-avian dinosaurs most closely related to birds.
facts.quote: Filogenéticamente, Deinonychosauria es el grupo de dinosaurios no avianos más cercano a las aves

facts.statement: A 2015 analysis by paleontologists Robert DePalma, David Burnham, Larry Martin, Peter Larson, and Robert Bakker places Deinonychus as basal in Dromaeosaurinae.
facts.quote: En un análisis de 2015 de los paleontólogos Robert DePalma, David Burnham, Larry Martin, Peter Larson y Robert Bakker, utilizando datos actualizados del Grupo de Trabajo Teróxido coloca a Deinonychus como basal en Dromaeosaurinae

facts.statement: The parent group of Deinonychus is Eudromaeosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eudromaeosauria

facts.statement: Deinonychus belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Deinonychus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Deinonychus lived from the Berriasian to the Cenomanian, between 143.1 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Cenomanian (143.1 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Velociraptor and its relatives used their claws rather than their skulls as hunting tools.
facts.quote: Velociraptor y sus parientes usaron sus garras más que sus cráneos como herramientas de caza
